weakest_inference: The load-bearing joint is Step 1's equality-squeeze at the substituted pair (x,y)=(f(t),t): it is the ONLY place both inequalities are used simultaneously and it generates the iterate identity f(f(t))=2f(t)-t on which Steps 2-5 entirely depend. I attacked it by factoring the squared gaps directly: C1 gap = (2ft-(fft+t))(2ft+(fft+t)) with the second factor strictly >0, so C1 <=> fft <= 2ft-t (upper bound); C2 gap = (fft+t-2ft)(fft+t+2ft) with the second factor strictly >0, so C2 <=> fft >= 2ft-t (lower bound). The two bounds coincide at 2ft-t, forcing equality. Both directions are justified because f(t),t>0 makes the pair admissible and every radicand/operand is strictly positive, so squaring is order-preserving. The squeeze is therefore airtight; it is the weakest link only in the sense of being the single most consequential inference, not because it is flawed.

summary: Second-order audit CONFIRMS the prior pass; the attack failed to overturn it. I independently reconstructed the full dependency graph: (C1),(C2) --squeeze at (f(t),t)--> iterate identity f(f(t))=2f(t)-t --(positivity of all iterates + recurrence)--> D=f-id>=0; (C2) --complete-the-square evaluated at u=f(s)--> master bound (3) D(v)<=D(s)+(v-s)^2/(4f(s)); (2)+(3)+swap --> derived continuity of D (Step 4, NO regularity assumed); (3)+compact minimum m=min f>0 --> |D(v)-D(s)|<=(v-s)^2/(4m) --n-partition telescoping--> D(q)=D(p) on every compact --> D global constant; codomain positivity --> c>=0. Every load-bearing algebraic identity was re-derived symbolically (both verification gaps=(x-y-c)^2; completing-the-square; recurrence closed form) and the squeeze was confirmed by direct factorization of both squared gaps. I reverse-checked every inequality direction (the strictly-positive cofactor means >=0 truly pins the decisive factor), tested existence/nonzero conclusions against 9 numerical candidate functions (only x+c feasible), and confirmed the master bound is tight for x+c and violated by all non-constant candidates. No circularity: continuity is DERIVED from (2)+(3), never assumed; (2) itself uses only f:R>0->R>0 and the iterate identity. No quantifier changes (all bounds hold for every s,v>0). No missing dependency and no required fix. The solution set f(x)=x+c, c>=0 is correct and the proof is complete and rigorous at IMO level.
